en: adv. separated by a distance or in pieces; not together; one from another; a. separate or distant; not together
ex: The two houses are about ten meters apart.
這兩棟房子相距約十公尺。

en: to tell someone that you are sorry for something you have done; to express regret
ex: I apologize for being late to the meeting.
對於開會遲到我深感抱歉。

en: n. a request for help, money or action; a formal request to a higher court to change a decision; the quality that makes people like something; v. to ask for something urgently; to ask a higher court to change a decision; to be attractive or interesting
ex: The charity made an appeal for donations.
慈善機構發出了募款的呼籲。

en: to officially agree to something; to have a good opinion of someone or something; to give permission for something
ex: The board approved the new budget.
董事會核准了新的預算。

en: n. a piece of clothing tied around the waist and worn over the front of your clothes to keep them clean, especially when cooking
ex: She put on an apron before she started cooking.
她開始煮飯前先繫上圍裙。

en: v. (of the police) to take someone away because they are suspected of a crime; to stop something happening or developing; to attract someone's attention; n. the act of arresting someone
ex: The police arrested the thief at the train station.
警方在火車站逮捕了小偷。

en: adv. to one side; in a different direction; used for saying something to yourself or to the audience; n. a remark made in a low voice that other people are not supposed to hear; a comment in a play
ex: She put her book aside and answered the phone.
她把書放到一旁去接電話。

en: v. to help someone to do something; to be present as a helper; n. (sports) a pass that leads directly to a score
ex: Volunteers assisted the elderly in crossing the street.
志工協助老人過馬路。

en: n. a person who helps someone more senior with their work; a person whose job is to help someone; a. next in rank below the person with the main responsibility
ex: The manager asked her assistant to book a meeting room.
經理請助理預訂一間會議室。

en: v. to accept something to be true without proof; to take on a responsibility or role; to start to have a particular appearance or quality; to pretend to feel something
ex: I assume that you've already read the report.
我猜想你已經讀過報告了。

en: n. a person who is good at sports or who takes part in sports competitions, especially running and jumping
ex: The young athlete trained every day for the Olympics.
這位年輕運動員為了奧運每天訓練。

en: n. the way that you think and feel about something or someone; the way you behave toward someone that shows how you feel; a position of the body; (informal) a bold or rude way of behaving
ex: She has a positive attitude toward life.
她對生活抱持積極的態度。

en: to make someone interested in something or someone; to pull something toward itself; to cause someone or something to come to a place; to be attractive
ex: The museum attracts thousands of visitors every year.
博物館每年吸引數千名遊客。

en: a. pleasant to look at; interesting or tempting; having qualities that people like
ex: She is an attractive woman with a warm smile.
她是個笑容溫暖、有魅力的女性。

en: a. (of a machine) working by itself without direct human control; (of an action) done without thinking; happening as a natural result; n. a gun that fires continuously when the trigger is pulled; a car with automatic gears
ex: The door opens automatically when you walk toward it.
當你走近時，門會自動打開。

en: n. (US) a road vehicle with an engine, usually with four wheels, for carrying a small number of people
ex: The automobile industry employs millions of workers.
汽車產業僱用了數百萬名工人。

en: a. not sleeping; v. (formal) to wake up or to wake someone up; to become aware of something
ex: The baby is awake and wants some milk.
寶寶醒了，想喝牛奶。

en: v. to wake someone up from sleep; to make someone realize something; to make someone feel or aware of something; to wake up
ex: The noise awakened the whole neighborhood.
噪音吵醒了整個街區。

en: n. a prize or other honor given for good work; a decision made by a judge; the amount of money decided by a court; v. to give something to someone as an official prize, payment or honor
ex: She won an award for best actress.
她獲頒最佳女主角獎。

en: a. knowing about something; having knowledge or understanding of a situation or fact; (aware of) conscious of something
ex: Are you aware of the risks involved?
你知道其中的風險嗎？
ph: as far as I am aware

en: a. very bad or unpleasant; (informal) very great; (old use) causing a feeling of respect and fear
ex: The weather was awful, so we stayed home all day.
天氣糟透了，所以我們整天待在家裡。

en: a. making you feel embarrassed and uncomfortable; moving in a clumsy way; difficult to use or deal with; difficult or inconvenient
ex: There was an awkward silence after her question.
她提問後出現一陣尷尬的沉默。

en: n. the part of a picture or scene behind the main objects; the facts, events and conditions that explain something; a person's family, education and experience
ex: His background in engineering helped him get the job.
他的工程背景讓他得到了這份工作。

en: n. very small living things that can only be seen with a microscope, some of which cause disease; (plural of bacterium)
ex: Wash your hands to get rid of bacteria.
洗手可以去除細菌。

en: adv. in a way that is not good enough; very much; to a serious degree; (informal) with great desire
ex: The team played badly and lost the game.
球隊打得很差，輸掉了比賽。

en: n. the cases and bags that someone carries with them when they travel; (informal) unwanted emotional experiences from the past
ex: Please collect your baggage at the carousel.
請到行李轉盤領取您的行李。

en: n. a tall tropical plant of the grass family with hard hollow stems that is used for building and making furniture
ex: Pandas eat bamboo all day long.
熊貓整天都在吃竹子。

en: a. not covered by clothes or anything else; (of a place) with little or nothing in it; plain and without decoration; v. to uncover something; to show something
ex: The children ran through the grass with bare feet.
孩子們赤腳跑過草地。

en: adv. only just; almost not; in a way that is not complete; (formal) in a bare or plain way
ex: I could barely hear what she was saying.
我幾乎聽不到她在說什麼。

en: n. a room or area in a building that is below ground level; the lowest part of a building
ex: They keep their old furniture in the basement.
他們把舊家具放在地下室。

en: n. an insect with a hard shell-like cover on its back, such as a ladybug or a weevil; (vi.) to move quickly; a heavy hammer
ex: A black beetle crawled across the floor.
一隻黑色甲蟲爬過地板。

en: n. a good or helpful result or effect; money or help given by the government or a company; v. to help someone or something; to receive an advantage from something
ex: Regular exercise has many benefits for your health.
規律運動對健康有許多好處。

en: prep. in addition to someone or something; not including; adv. also; used to give a further reason
ex: Besides English, she speaks French and Japanese.
除了英文之外，她還會說法文和日文。

en: v. to tie something together with string or rope; to force someone to obey a law or promise; to fasten pages together into a book; to stick together; n. (informal) a difficult situation
ex: He used a rope to bind the boxes together.
他用繩子把箱子綁在一起。

en: v. to ask God to protect someone or something; to make something holy; to give someone a gift or talent; (in the phrase 'bless you') to say something after someone sneezes
ex: The priest blessed the new couple.
神父祝福這對新人。

en: a. covered with blood; with a lot of violence and killing; (BrE informal) used for emphasis, often in anger
ex: The film contains a lot of bloody fight scenes.
這部電影有許多血腥的打鬥場面。

en: n. a loose piece of clothing like a shirt that is worn by women or girls
ex: She wore a white blouse with a long black skirt.
她穿著白襯衫配黑色長裙。

en: n. a device that explodes and causes damage; the act of attacking with these devices; (informal) a complete failure; v. to attack a place with bombs; (informal) to fail badly
ex: The bomb exploded in the empty building.
炸彈在空樓裡爆炸。

en: n. a strong shoe that covers the foot and ankle; (BrE) the space at the back of a car for baggage; v. to kick something hard; (informal) to force someone to leave a job; to start a computer
ex: He put on his boots before going out into the snow.
他出門踏雪前先穿上靴子。

en: v. to make someone feel tired and uninterested by being dull; to make a hole in something with a tool; n. someone or something that is very dull; a wave of water that rushes up a river; the hollow part of a gun barrel
ex: The long speech bored the audience.
冗長的演講讓觀眾覺得很無聊。
